30-60-90-triangle: A right triangle with angles of $30^\circ$, $60^\circ$, and $90^\circ$. If the short leg is $x$, the long leg is $x\sqrt{3}$ and the hypotenuse is $2x$.
45-45-90-triangle: A right triangle with two $45^\circ$ angles. Its legs are equal, and the hypotenuse is the leg times $\sqrt{2}$.
aa-similarity: If two angles of one triangle are equal to two angles of another triangle, the triangles are similar.
aas: Angle, angle, side. If two angles and a side that is not between them in one triangle are congruent to the matching parts of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
acute-angle: An angle that measures more than $0^\circ$ and less than $90^\circ$.
adjacent-angles: Two angles that share a vertex and one side, and do not overlap.
adjacent-side: In a right triangle, the leg that touches a chosen acute angle. (The hypotenuse touches it too, but it is not called adjacent.)
alternate-exterior-angles: Two angles outside the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, alternate exterior angles are equal.
alternate-interior-angles: Two angles between the two lines, on opposite sides of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, alternate interior angles are equal.
angle: Two rays with the same endpoint. The endpoint is the vertex. Write $\angle ABC$, with the vertex in the middle.
angle-bisector: A ray that starts at the vertex of an angle and cuts the angle into two congruent angles.
angle-of-depression: The angle from the horizontal down to a line of sight. It equals the angle of elevation from the lower point to the higher point.
angle-of-elevation: The angle from the horizontal up to a line of sight.
angle-of-rotation: The amount a figure turns in a rotation, in degrees. Counterclockwise turns are positive.
annulus: The ring-shaped region between two circles with the same center. Its area is $\pi R^2 - \pi r^2$, where $R$ is the outer radius and $r$ is the inner radius.
apothem: The distance from the center of a regular polygon to the middle of a side. It is perpendicular to that side.
arc: Part of a circle between two points on the circle. Two points split a circle into a minor arc and a major arc (or two semicircles).
arc-length: The distance along an arc. It is a length, in units such as inches or meters. Arc length $= \dfrac{\text{central angle}}{360^\circ} \cdot 2\pi r$.
arc-measure: The size of an arc in degrees. It equals the measure of its central angle. A semicircle measures $180^\circ$. A circle measures $360^\circ$ all the way around.
area: The number of square units inside a figure.
asa: Angle, side, angle. If two angles and the included side of one triangle are congruent to two angles and the included side of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
axis-of-revolution: The line that a flat shape spins around to make a solid of revolution.
base-angles: The two angles of an isosceles triangle that touch the base. Base angles are congruent.
base-of-a-polygon: The side of a parallelogram, triangle, or trapezoid that you measure the height to. You can choose any side as the base.
base-of-an-isosceles-triangle: The side of an isosceles triangle that is not one of the two congruent sides.
bounding-box: The smallest rectangle with sides on grid lines that has a figure inside it. It is used to find area by subtracting the corner pieces.
cavalieris-principle: If two solids have the same height and the same cross-section area at every level, they have the same volume.
center-of-a-circle: The point inside a circle that is the same distance from every point on the circle. We name a circle by its center.
center-of-dilation: The fixed point a dilation moves points toward or away from. Each point and its image are on a ray from the center.
center-of-rotation: The fixed point a figure turns about in a rotation.
central-angle: An angle whose vertex is the center of a circle. Its sides are two radii.
chord: A segment with both endpoints on a circle. A diameter is a chord that goes through the center.
circle: All the points in a plane that are the same distance from one point, the center. We write circle $P$ as $\odot P$.
circumference: The distance around a circle. $C = \pi d = 2\pi r$.
collinear: Points that lie on the same line.
compass: A tool that draws arcs and circles. The width of the compass stays the same while you draw, so every point on the arc is the same distance from the center.
complementary: Two angles whose measures add to $90^\circ$. Each angle is the complement of the other.
completing-the-square: A way to rewrite $x^2 + bx$ as a perfect square by adding $\left(\dfrac{b}{2}\right)^2$. Add the same number to both sides of an equation.
composite-figure: A figure made of two or more simple shapes. Find its area by adding the areas of the parts, or by subtracting a part from a larger shape.
cone: A solid with one circle as its base and a curved surface that comes to a point, the apex.
congruence-statement: A statement such as $\triangle ABC \cong \triangle FDE$. The order of the letters shows which parts correspond: $A$ matches $F$, $B$ matches $D$, and $C$ matches $E$.
congruent: Having the same size and shape. Congruent segments have the same length. Congruent angles have the same measure. The symbol is $\cong$.
consecutive-angles: Two angles of a polygon that share a side. In a parallelogram, consecutive angles are supplementary.
construction: A drawing made with only a compass and a straightedge. A construction uses no ruler and no protractor.
converse: The statement you get by turning an “if, then” rule around.
convex-polygon: A polygon where every segment between two points of the polygon stays inside it. A polygon that is not convex is concave. A concave polygon has a corner that points inward.
coordinate-plane: A flat surface with a horizontal $x$-axis and a vertical $y$-axis. Every point has an ordered pair $(x, y)$.
coordinate-proof: A way to show a fact for sure by using coordinates, slopes, and distances instead of a picture. Also called computation as proof.
coplanar: Points or lines that lie in the same plane.
corresponding-angles: Two angles in the same position at the two places where a transversal crosses two lines. If the two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal.
corresponding-parts: The sides and angles that match when one figure is moved onto a congruent figure. Corresponding parts of congruent figures are congruent.
cosine: For an acute angle $A$ in a right triangle, $\cos A = \dfrac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$.
counterexample: One example that shows a statement is not always true.
cross-products: In the proportion $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{c}{d}$, the products $a \cdot d$ and $b \cdot c$. They are equal.
cross-section: The flat shape you see when a plane slices through a solid.
cubic-unit: A cube with edges of length $1$ unit. Volume counts how many cubic units fill a solid. Examples are cubic inches, cubic feet, and cubic yards.
cylinder: A solid with two parallel circles as bases and one curved surface between them.
degree: The unit for measuring angles, written $^\circ$. A full turn is $360^\circ$. A right angle is $90^\circ$.
density: How much mass is packed into each unit of volume: $\text{density} = \dfrac{\text{mass}}{\text{volume}}$. Weight is found by multiplying density by volume.
diagonal: A segment that joins two corners of a polygon that are not next to each other.
diameter: A chord that goes through the center of a circle. Its length is twice the radius: $d = 2r$.
dilation: A transformation that makes a figure larger or smaller from a fixed point, the center of dilation. It keeps the shape and angles but multiplies every length by the scale factor.
distance-formula: The distance between $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$ is $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$.
edge: A segment where two faces of a polyhedron meet. A cube has 12 edges.
endpoint: A point at the end of a segment or the start of a ray.
enlargement: A dilation with a scale factor greater than 1. The image is larger than the original.
equation-of-a-circle: The equation $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$ describes a circle with center $(h, k)$ and radius $r$.
equiangular: Having all angles the same measure. An equiangular triangle has three $60^\circ$ angles.
equilateral-triangle: A triangle with all three sides the same length. Each angle measures $60^\circ$.
eulers-formula: For a polyhedron with no holes, $F + V - E = 2$. $F$ is the number of faces, $V$ the number of vertices, and $E$ the number of edges.
exterior-angle: An angle outside a polygon, made by one side and the extension of the next side. An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles.
face: A flat surface of a polyhedron. A cube has 6 faces.
frustum: A cone or pyramid with the top cut off by a plane parallel to the base. Find its volume by subtracting the small cone (or pyramid) from the large one.
height-of-a-polygon: The distance from the base to the opposite side (or opposite vertex), measured at a right angle to the base. It is not the length of a slanted side.
hemisphere: Half of a sphere. Its volume is $\frac{2}{3}\pi r^3$.
hl: Hypotenuse, leg. If the hypotenuse and a leg of one right triangle are congruent to the hypotenuse and a leg of another right triangle, the triangles are congruent. HL works for right triangles only.
hypotenuse: The side of a right triangle across from the right angle. It is the longest side.
image: The new figure after a transformation. The image of point $A$ is named $A'$ and is read “A prime”.
included-angle: The angle between two sides of a triangle. It is formed by those two sides.
included-side: The side between two angles of a triangle. It connects the vertices of those two angles.
indirect-measurement: Finding a length that is hard to measure by using similar triangles and lengths that are easy to measure.
inscribed-angle: An angle with its vertex on a circle and both sides chords of the circle. Its measure is half of its intercepted arc.
inscribed-quadrilateral: A four-sided figure with all four vertices on a circle. Its opposite angles are supplementary.
intercepted-arc: The arc that lies inside an inscribed or central angle, between its two sides.
intersect: To cross or meet. Two lines intersect at a point. Two planes intersect in a line.
inverse-cosine: The angle whose cosine is a given number. Write $\cos^{-1}(x)$. The $-1$ is not an exponent.
inverse-sine: The angle whose sine is a given number. Write $\sin^{-1}(x)$. The $-1$ is not an exponent.
inverse-tangent: The angle whose tangent is a given number. Write $\tan^{-1}(x)$. The $-1$ is not an exponent.
isosceles-trapezoid: A trapezoid whose legs are congruent. Each pair of base angles is congruent, and the diagonals are congruent.
isosceles-triangle: A triangle with at least two sides the same length. The angles across from the equal sides are equal.
kite: A quadrilateral with two pairs of congruent sides that are next to each other. The diagonals are perpendicular.
lateral-area: The area of the sides of a solid, without the base or bases.
leg: One of the two sides of a right triangle that form the right angle.
legs-of-an-isosceles-triangle: The two congruent sides of an isosceles triangle.
like-radicals: Radicals with the same radicand. You can add them: $3\sqrt{2} + 5\sqrt{2} = 8\sqrt{2}$.
line: A straight path of points that goes on forever in both directions. Write $\overleftrightarrow{AB}$ or name it with one small letter, like line $\ell$.
line-of-reflection: The line a figure is flipped over in a reflection. It is the perpendicular bisector of the segment from each point to its image.
line-of-symmetry: A line that divides a figure into two halves that are mirror images of each other.
line-symmetry: A figure has line symmetry if a reflection over a line maps the figure onto itself.
linear-pair: Two adjacent angles whose outside sides are opposite rays. The angles in a linear pair are supplementary.
major-arc: An arc that is more than half of a circle. Its measure is more than $180^\circ$. We name it with three letters.
measure-of-an-angle: How far an angle opens, in degrees. Write $m\angle ABC = 40^\circ$. Read it as “the measure of angle $ABC$ is 40 degrees.”
midpoint: The point exactly halfway between the endpoints of a segment. It cuts the segment into two congruent segments.
midsegment-of-a-trapezoid: The segment that connects the midpoints of the two legs of a trapezoid. It is parallel to the bases. Its length is the average of the base lengths.
midsegment-of-a-triangle: A segment that joins the midpoints of two sides of a triangle. It is parallel to the third side and half as long.
minor-arc: An arc that is less than half of a circle. Its measure is less than $180^\circ$. We name it with its two endpoints.
net: A flat pattern that folds up into a solid. A net shows every face of the solid.
oblique: Slanted. In an oblique prism or cylinder, the sides lean over and are not at a right angle to the bases. The height is still measured straight up, at a right angle to the bases.
obtuse-angle: An angle that measures more than $90^\circ$ and less than $180^\circ$.
opposite-rays: Two rays with the same endpoint that go in opposite directions. Together they make a line.
opposite-reciprocal: The number you get by flipping a fraction and changing its sign. Slopes of perpendicular lines are opposite reciprocals.
opposite-side: In a right triangle, the leg across from a chosen acute angle. It does not touch that angle.
order-of-rotational-symmetry: The number of times a figure fits onto itself in one full turn. The smallest angle of rotation is $\dfrac{360^\circ}{n}$ when the order is $n$.
orientation: The order, clockwise or counterclockwise, in which the labeled points of a figure go around. A reflection reverses orientation.
parallel: Parallel lines are in the same plane and never meet. They stay the same distance apart. The symbol is $\parallel$. In a figure, matching arrows mark parallel lines.
parallelogram: A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
partition: To divide a segment into parts. A point partitions a segment in the ratio $a:b$ when the two parts have lengths in the ratio $a$ to $b$.
perfect-square: A number that is the square of a whole number, such as 1, 4, 9, 16, 25.
perimeter: The distance around a polygon. It is the sum of the side lengths.
perpendicular: Perpendicular lines cross to make right angles. The symbol is $\perp$.
perpendicular-bisector: A line that goes through the midpoint of a segment and is perpendicular to it.
pi: The number $\pi$ is the circumference of a circle divided by its diameter. It is the same for every circle. $\pi \approx 3.14159$.
plane: A flat surface that goes on forever in every direction. Name it with one capital letter, like plane $P$, or with three points in it that are not on one line.
point: An exact location. A point has no size. Name it with a capital letter, like point $A$.
point-of-tangency: The one point where a tangent line touches a circle.
polygon: A closed figure made of three or more segments, called sides, that meet only at their endpoints. A polygon with $n$ sides is an $n$-gon. The angles of a polygon with $n$ sides add to $(n - 2) \cdot 180^\circ$.
polyhedron: A solid whose faces are all flat polygons. Prisms and pyramids are polyhedrons. Cylinders, cones, and spheres are not.
population-density: The number of people living in each unit of area, such as people per square mile: $\dfrac{\text{population}}{\text{area}}$.
preimage: The original figure, before a transformation.
prism: A polyhedron with two parallel, congruent faces called bases. The other faces are parallelograms. A prism is named by its base, such as a triangular prism.
proportion: An equation that says two ratios are equal.
proportional: Two lists of numbers are proportional when the ratios of matching numbers are all equal.
protractor: A tool that measures angles in degrees. It has an outer scale and an inner scale. Read the scale that starts at $0$ on one side of the angle.
pyramid: A polyhedron with one polygon base. The other faces are triangles that meet at one vertex, the apex.
pythagorean-theorem: In a right triangle, the sum of the squares of the legs equals the square of the hypotenuse: $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
pythagorean-triple: Three whole numbers $a$, $b$, $c$ with $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$.
quadrilateral: A polygon with four sides. The four angles add to $360^\circ$.
radian: A unit for measuring angles. One radian is the central angle whose arc is as long as the radius. A full turn is $2\pi$ radians, so $180^\circ = \pi$ radians. Radian measure $\theta = \dfrac{s}{r}$.
radical: An expression with a root sign, such as $\sqrt{50}$ or $3\sqrt{2}$. The number under the sign is the radicand.
radicand: The number under a radical sign. In $\sqrt{50}$ the radicand is 50.
radius: A segment from the center of a circle to a point on the circle. It is also the length of that segment. The plural is radii. All radii of a circle are equal.
ratio: A comparison of two numbers by division. It can be written $a : b$, $\dfrac{a}{b}$, or “a to b”.
rationalize: To rewrite a fraction so that the denominator has no radical.
ray: Part of a line that starts at one endpoint and goes on forever in one direction. Write $\overrightarrow{AB}$: it starts at $A$ and goes through $B$.
rectangle: A parallelogram with a right angle.
reduction: A dilation with a scale factor between 0 and 1. The image is smaller than the original.
reflection: A transformation that flips a figure over a line. Each point and its image are the same distance from the line, on opposite sides.
regular-polygon: A polygon with all sides the same length and all angles the same measure.
rhombus: A quadrilateral with four sides of equal length.
right-angle: An angle that measures exactly $90^\circ$. A small square at the vertex marks a right angle.
rigid-motion: A transformation that keeps all lengths and all angle measures the same. Translations, reflections, and rotations are rigid motions.
rotation: A transformation that turns every point of a figure by the same angle about a fixed point, the center of rotation.
rotational-symmetry: A figure has rotational symmetry if a rotation of less than $360^\circ$ about its center maps the figure onto itself.
same-side-interior-angles: Two angles between the two lines, on the same side of the transversal. If the two lines are parallel, same-side interior angles are supplementary.
sas: Side, angle, side. If two sides and the included angle of one triangle are congruent to two sides and the included angle of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
sas-similarity: If two pairs of matching sides are proportional and the included angles are equal, the triangles are similar.
scale: The ratio that compares a length on a drawing or map to the real length.
scale-drawing: A drawing that has the same shape as the real object but a different size. Maps and floor plans are scale drawings.
scale-factor: The number $k$ that a dilation multiplies every length by. It equals $\dfrac{\text{image length}}{\text{original length}}$.
scalene-triangle: A triangle with no two sides the same length.
sector: The region inside a circle between two radii and the arc they cut off. Area $= \dfrac{\text{central angle}}{360^\circ} \cdot \pi r^2$.
segment: Part of a line between two endpoints. Write $\overline{AB}$. Its length is written $AB$, with no bar.
segment-bisector: A point, line, ray, or segment that goes through the midpoint of a segment.
semicircle: Half of a circle. It is an arc that measures $180^\circ$. The endpoints of a semicircle are the ends of a diameter.
sequence-of-transformations: Two or more transformations done one after another. The first image is $A'$ and the second image is $A''$.
shaded-region: A part of a figure that is colored in. To find its area, add or subtract the areas of simple shapes.
similar: Figures that have the same shape but not always the same size. Matching angles are equal and matching sides are proportional. The symbol is $\sim$.
similarity-statement: A statement such as $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF$. The order of the letters shows which vertices match.
sine: For an acute angle $A$ in a right triangle, $\sin A = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$.
skew: Skew lines are not in the same plane. They do not meet and they are not parallel.
slant-height: For a pyramid, the height of a triangle face, measured along the face from the base edge to the apex. For a cone, the distance along the surface from the edge of the base to the apex. It is written $\ell$.
slope: A number that tells how steep a line is: the change in $y$ divided by the change in $x$, or rise over run.
solid: A three-dimensional shape. It takes up space.
solid-of-revolution: A solid made by spinning a flat shape around a line.
special-right-triangle: A right triangle whose sides follow a pattern you can use without a calculator. The two special right triangles are the $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle and the $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangle.
sphere: The set of all points in space that are the same distance (the radius) from one point, the center. A ball is a sphere.
square: A quadrilateral that is both a rectangle and a rhombus: four equal sides and four right angles.
square-root: A number that gives the original number when you multiply it by itself. In geometry we use the positive root.
sss: Side, side, side. If three sides of one triangle are congruent to three sides of another triangle, the triangles are congruent.
sss-similarity: If the three pairs of matching sides of two triangles are proportional, the triangles are similar.
straight-angle: An angle that measures exactly $180^\circ$. Its sides are opposite rays, so it looks like a line.
straightedge: A tool for drawing straight lines. A straightedge has no number marks.
supplementary: Two angles whose measures add to $180^\circ$. Each angle is the supplement of the other.
surface-area: The total area of all the faces (or the whole outside surface) of a solid. It is measured in square units.
tangent: For an acute angle $A$ in a right triangle, $\tan A = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$. It is the slope of a line that makes angle $A$ with the horizontal.
tangent-to-a-circle: A line in the plane of a circle that touches the circle at exactly one point. It is perpendicular to the radius at that point. Two tangent segments from one outside point are equal.
transformation: A rule that moves or changes every point of a figure. Translations, reflections, rotations, and dilations are transformations.
translation: A transformation that slides every point of a figure the same distance in the same direction. It does not turn or flip the figure.
transversal: A line that crosses two or more other lines at different points.
trapezoid: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides. The parallel sides are the bases. The other two sides are the legs.
triangle: A polygon with three sides and three angles. The angles of a triangle add to $180^\circ$. Write $\triangle ABC$.
triangle-inequality: The two shorter sides of a triangle always add to more than the longest side.
trigonometric-ratio: A ratio of two sides of a right triangle. The three trigonometric ratios are sine, cosine, and tangent. Each depends only on the acute angle.
vertex: The point where the two sides of an angle meet. The plural is vertices.
vertex-angle: The angle of an isosceles triangle between the two congruent sides.
vertex-of-a-solid: A point where three or more edges of a polyhedron meet. A cube has 8 vertices. The plural is vertices.
vertical-angles: The two angles across from each other when two lines cross. Vertical angles are equal.
volume: The amount of space inside a solid. It is measured in cubic units.
